---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Persistent Liquidity EBITDA Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lct), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their cash surplus over short-term debt has remained adequate relative to current liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The best prior evidence came from operating-value anchors paired with near-term liquidity, but a single-period liquidity cushion may reflect temporary cash timing. Using the three-period minimum tests whether cheap EBITDA is supported by persistent liquidity rather than a one-time balance-sheet snapshot.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Net-Cash-Quality OCF Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), act)))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow yield should be most valuable when current assets remain cash-rich after subtracting debt due within one year.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This refines the strong OCF-yield plus cash-quality evidence by incorporating the immediate debt claim against cash. Cheap operating cash flow is more likely to accrue to equity holders when current assets are not only liquid but liquid net of near-term debt repayment needs.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Liquidity-Shortfall Adjusted OCF Yield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(oancf, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), MAX(dlc, SUB(lct, che))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow cheapness should predict returns better after penalizing firms whose equity value is low because of a near-term liquidity shortfall.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is not a full enterprise-value multiple; it adds only the larger of debt due soon and current-liability cash shortfall to the equity valuation base. Firms with high OCF relative to this adjusted claim base should be cheap cash generators rather than equity stubs facing imminent creditor pressure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cash-Quality Maturity OCF Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, act), NEG(RATIO(dlc, lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: OCF-cheap firms should outperform when current assets are cash-heavy and current liabilities are not dominated by debt due soon.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The distress leg combines two non-identical claim-quality dimensions: liquid asset composition and maturity-wall intensity. This tests whether cash-flow cheapness is strongest when both the asset side and liability side of the current balance sheet reduce distress risk.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Weakest-Link OCF Safety Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(MIN(RATIO(che, lct), RATIO(ceq, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow yield should be rewarded when both immediate cash coverage and balance-sheet equity cushion are adequate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cheap cash-flow firms can still be value traps if either near-term liquidity or broader solvency is the binding constraint. The minimum operator makes the distress conditioner depend on the weaker of cash-to-current-liabilities and equity-to-liabilities, rather than allowing one safety dimension to mask severe weakness in the other.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Cash-Quality EBITDA Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, act)))
HYPOTHESIS: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their current assets are concentrated in cash rather than less reliable working-capital assets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: EBITDA yield has been the most successful valuation anchor, while cash-heavy current assets showed strong evidence when paired with OCF yield. This signal tests whether the cash-quality mechanism generalizes to operating earnings cheapness without relying on the prior cash-minus-debt-over-current-liabilities liquidity screen.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

response:
---CRITIQUE Persistent Liquidity EBITDA Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a cosmetic temporal-smoothing variant of the archive's best performer (Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value, same EBITDA/ME × (che−dlc)/lct construction) with TS_MIN(...,3) substituted for the contemporaneous level, and it will mainly reduce coverage rather than test a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Net-Cash-Quality OCF Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The conditioner is an interpolation between two already-tested archive conditioners ((che−dlc)/lct in Cash-Buffered OCF Yield and che/act in Cash-Quality OCF Yield) applied to the identical OCF-yield anchor, so it is a denominator/numerator tweak rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Liquidity-Shortfall Adjusted OCF Yield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It is close to the archive's failed Creditor-Claim Earnings Yield template and edges toward a plain cash-flow-to-enterprise-value multiple, but the MAX(dlc, lct−che) shortfall adjustment is a genuinely different functional form (a single levered yield rather than a rank interaction) with defensible sign direction and high coverage, so it is worth one test.

---CRITIQUE Cash-Quality Maturity OCF Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: It bolts a conditioner already shown to be near-useless in the archive (dlc-share of liabilities, e.g. Long-Runway EBITDA Value with ls_alpha −0.002) onto the proven che/act conditioner via SUMRANK, which most likely just dilutes the known effect rather than isolating anything new.

---CRITIQUE Weakest-Link OCF Safety Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated "weaker of two safety dimensions" logic fails because MIN is applied to unranked ratios on very different level scales (che/lct typically well below ceq/lt), so the conditioner will almost always collapse to cash-to-current-liabilities and the expression does not compute the hypothesized weakest-link comparison.

---CRITIQUE Cash-Quality EBITDA Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A modest but legitimate cross-check of whether the strong che/act cash-composition conditioner generalizes from the OCF anchor to the higher-coverage EBITDA anchor (0.14 vs 0.079), which is an untested pairing with a real coverage-driven motivation rather than a pure relabeling.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Liability-Scale EBITDA Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(sale, lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: EBITDA-cheap firms should outperform when their operating sales base is large relative to total liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This moves away from another temporal version of the cash-minus-short-debt liquidity screen. The distress leg asks whether creditor claims are supported by ongoing business scale, so high EBITDA yield is less likely to represent a thin equity stub behind excessive liabilities.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Loss-Runway OCF Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(lct, MAX(NEG(pi), 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow cheapness should be more reliable when cash can cover both near-term liabilities and any current pretax loss drain.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This is not an interpolation between cash-quality and cash-minus-debt conditioners; it measures survival runway against explicit current claims plus operating losses. Cheap operating cash flow is more likely to accrue to shareholders when the firm has enough cash to avoid forced financing while distress is being resolved.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Noncash-Asset-Drag OCF Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: OCF-cheap firms should outperform when current assets are not dominated by noncash working-capital items relative to sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This removes the weak debt-maturity-share add-on and instead tests whether cash-flow cheapness is contaminated by receivable or inventory bloat. A low noncash-current-asset burden makes reported operating cash flow more likely to be a durable value signal rather than a temporary artifact of strained working-capital management.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Percentile Weakest-Link OCF Safety
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(che, lct)), RANK(RATIO(ceq, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-cash-flow yield should be rewarded only when both immediate liquidity and broader solvency are reasonably strong.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Ranking each safety dimension before applying MIN fixes the scale problem and makes the conditioner a true weakest-link comparison. Cheap cash-flow firms are penalized if either cash coverage of current liabilities or equity coverage of total liabilities is weak, because either constraint can turn value into distress.
